record.context_brief: Explicit RH upper bound for zeta moments
record.original_question: Let Ik(T) = integral from 0 to T of |zeta(1/2 + it)|^(2k) dt. Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, determine an explicit constant Ck, for each real k > 0, such that Ik(T) <= Ck T (log T)^(k^2) for all sufficiently large T.

evidence.quote: Give an explicit version of Harper’s [40] upper bound for Ik (T ), assuming the Riemann hypothesis. That is, for k > 0 determine Ck such that Ik (T ) <= Ck T (log T )^(k^2) for T sufficiently large.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For real $k>0$ and $T\geq 2$, define the $2k$-th moment of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line by
$$I_k(T) \;=\; \int_0^T \bigl|\zeta\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}+it\right)\bigr|^{2k}\,dt.$$
Assume the Riemann Hypothesis (i.e. all non-trivial zeros of $\zeta(s)$ have real part $1/2$). It is known that under this assumption one has $I_k(T) \ll_k T(\log T)^{k^2}$ for every $k>0$, with an implicit constant depending on $k$.

Problem: For each real $k>0$, determine an explicit numerical constant $C_k$ (given by a closed-form expression in $k$) such that
$$I_k(T) \;\leq\; C_k\, T\,(\log T)^{k^2}$$
holds for all sufficiently large $T$. The goal is to make $C_k$ as small and as explicit as possible as a function of $k$.
artifact.category_tag: Moments of the Riemann zeta function
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (arXiv:2407.20023, 2024) optimizes the implicit constant in Harper's conditional upper bound and obtains an explicit $C_k = O(\exp(\exp(18.63 k)))$, by making each step in Harper's argument quantitative. So an explicit (though large) admissible $C_k$ is now known; finding the optimal/best explicit constant remains a subject of ongoing improvement, hence partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Optimization of the Implicit Constant for Upper Bounds for Moments of the Riemann zeta Function
status_evidence.snippet: They obtain an explicit constant C(k) = O(e^{e^{18.63k}}) in Harper's conditional upper bound I_k(T) <= C_k T (log T)^{k^2}.
status_evidence.claim: An explicit constant C_k has been worked out, of size doubly exponential in k.

status_evidence.title: Moments of L-functions problem list
status_evidence.snippet: Give an explicit version of Harper's upper bound for I_k(T), assuming RH; that is, determine C_k such that I_k(T) <= C_k T (log T)^{k^2}.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of making Harper's constant explicit is listed as an open/active research problem.
